answer: Consider attestation backed by hardware oracles. Each agent controls a unique sealed device that emits a signed heartbeat, a pulse accepted once per epoch. Fake agents cannot manufacture extra hearts, so spawning a thousand identities buys nothing. Rewards accrue per oracle, forcing attackers to buy real units instead of forging keys: a walnut-sized chip that is cheap to make but impossible to clone. Reputation settles like a marble rolling downhill: honest oracles gain weight, duplicates stall and wash out, pushing payoff per fake identity below hardware cost and killing the attack's profit.
